validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION confirmed independently of GEM. Equitrans, L.P.'s FERC-regulated interstate transmission-and-storage system ('the mainline Equitrans, L.P. system') is documented in Equitrans Midstream Corp's FY2023 10-K (SEC EDGAR, CIK 1747009, filed 2024-02-20) and in EQT Corporation's FY2025 10-K (SEC EDGAR, CIK 33213, filed 2026-02-18, post the 2024-07-22 Equitrans Midstream Merger) as ~940-950 miles of FERC-regulated interstate pipeline with interconnects to seven interstate pipelines, in northern WV / southwestern PA / southeastern OH. The company's own FERC open-season exhibit (Equitrans, L.P., Docket CP22- (OVCX), Exhibit Z-3, 'Equitrans 2021 System Expansion', April 2021 non-binding notice, archived via Wayback since ovcx.info is now unreachable) repeatedly names the 'Equitrans Mainline System' by that exact name and describes it as overlaying 'the heart of the Marcellus and Utica shale in north central West Virginia, southwestern Pennsylvania, and eastern Ohio' -- this independently corroborates existence, classification (transmission, not gathering), and FuelSource. Classified correctly as 'transmission': both the 10-Ks and the OVCX exhibit consistently describe a FERC-regulated interstate transmission-and-storage system, distinct from Equitrans' separately-described gathering system. CAVEAT: the row's segment_name 'Equitrans Mainline' with both endpoints blank functions, in company usage, as shorthand for the whole backbone system (which is fed by laterals including the Ohio Valley Connector (P6897) and Sunrise Transmission System) rather than one bounded pipe segment -- see the companion spec concern below on Capacity for the resulting system-vs-segment conflation shared with P6896/P6897.

validity.recommendation: flag Capacity as a SYSTEM-level aggregate, not a segment rating, and update it to EQT's freshest disclosed figure (5,000 MMcf/d as of 2025-12-31) rather than the stale 2019-2022 figure of 4,400; the identical 4,400 MMcf/d figure is also carried on P6896 (Allegheny Valley Connector) and P6897 (Ohio Valley Connector), both individual laterals feeding INTO this system with their own much smaller true capacities
validity.researcher_notes: ORCHESTRATOR HEADLINE FINDING. The 4,400 MMcf/d recorded for P6895 (and identically for P6896 and P6897) is Equitrans' company-wide TOTAL THROUGHPUT CAPACITY for its entire transmission-and-storage system, not a rating of any single pipe or segment. Confirmed verbatim, word-for-word, across THREE separate company disclosures spanning three years: (1) Equitrans Midstream's OVCX Exhibit Z-3 (FERC Docket CP22-, filed 2021, 'About Equitrans Midstream Corporation' boilerplate) states, for both its April 2021 non-binding notice (YE2019 data) and June 2021 binding notice (YE2020 data): 'ETRN's transmission and storage system includes approximately 950 miles of FERC-regulated interstate pipelines... total throughput capacity of approximately 4.4 Bcf per day.' (2) The company's own transmission.html investor page (Wayback capture dated 2026-01-13, content dated 'As of December 31, 2022') restates it unchanged: 'the transmission and storage system included approximately 940 miles of FERC-regulated, interstate pipelines... with total throughput capacity of approximately 4.4 Bcf per day.' So the SAME 4.4 Bcf/d (=4,400 MMcf/d) figure for the WHOLE ~940-950 mile system was disclosed unchanged from 2019 through 2022 -- explaining why it landed identically on all three GEM rows that trace to this system. (3) It has since changed: EQT Corporation's FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-02-18, post the 2024-07-22 Equitrans Midstream Merger) gives a fresh 'as of December 31, 2025' system table for the same Transmission segment: 'Pipeline miles 950 / Throughput capacity (Bcf per day) 5.0 / Interconnect points 8 / Compression units 45 / Compression horsepower 197,000' -- i.e. the true CURRENT system aggregate is now 5.0 Bcf/d (5,000 MMcf/d), not 4.4 Bcf/d. So the recorded 4,400 is both (a) a system aggregate improperly applied to what reads as a segment row, and (b) stale by roughly four years. Independent cross-check: EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset (May 2018 release, 'Historical Projects' sheet, Excel row 13) records the Ohio Valley Connector itself (docket CP15-41, completed 2016-10, WV->OH, 50 mi, 30/24-inch) at its OWN additional capacity of 850 MMcf/d -- an order of magnitude below 4,400 -- which independently proves at least P6897 cannot legitimately carry the system figure. All three company documents above are Equitrans/EQT-family disclosures (one origin per the tier-discipline rule), so this is staged at tier medium / independent:false despite three separate documents/years -- an independent (non-Equitrand-family) confirmation of the CURRENT 5.0 Bcf/d figure was not found this session (WebSearch budget exhausted; only SEC EDGAR, local EIA CSVs and Wayback were reachable). Recommend the orchestrator treat P6895 as the row closest to representing this system aggregate (if any of the three should retain a system-level number, it is this one), while P6896 and P6897 should be re-sourced to their own segment-specific capacities (see cross_row_leads).

cross_row_leads.facts: EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects, May 2018 release, 'Historical Projects' sheet, Excel row 13: project 'Ohio Valley Connector', operator 'Equitrans', WV->OH, 50 miles, 30/24-inch diameter, docket CP15-41, completed 2016-10, additional capacity 850 MMcf/d, cost $415M. No project named 'Allegheny Valley Connector' (or the sheet's misspelled 'Allenghy Valley Connector') was found anywhere in the EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset (searched all 28 tracked releases by operator 'Equitrans'/'Equitrans LP' and by name -- zero hits for 'allegheny'), nor named as such in the ETRN/EQT 10-Ks or the OVCX Exhibit Z-3 (which does name the Sunrise Transmission System and the Ohio Valley Connector as Mainline receipt points, but never an 'Allegheny Valley Connector'). The 4,400 MMcf/d on P6896 is almost certainly the same Equitrans Mainline System aggregate throughput figure misapplied here (see P6895's validity/spec finding) rather than a sourced capacity specific to this project. Recommend the P6896 researcher independently source this lateral's own name/scope/capacity (FERC docket search under 'Equitrans' for an Allegheny-named project) rather than carrying the system figure forward, and correct the roster's spelling to 'Allegheny.'
